articles.title: Personal mobility and manipulation using robotics, artificial intelligence and advanced control.
articles.abstract: Recent advancements of technologies, including computation, robotics, machine learning, communication, and miniaturization technologies, bring us closer to futuristic visions of compassionate intelligent devices. The missing element is a basic understanding of how to relate human functions (physiological, physical, and cognitive) to the design of intelligent devices and systems that aid and interact with people. Our stakeholder and clinician consultants identified a number of mobility barriers that have been intransigent to traditional approaches. The most important physical obstacles are stairs, steps, curbs, doorways (doors), rough/uneven surfaces, weather hazards (snow, ice), crowded/cluttered spaces, and confined spaces. Focus group participants suggested a number of ways to make interaction simpler, including natural language interfaces such as the ability to say "I want a drink", a library of high level commands (open a door, park the wheelchair, ...), and a touchscreen interface with images so the user could point and use other gestures.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
scripts/research/retrieval_log.py — persist what was actually retrieved.

WHY
---
On 2026-08-19 the first research batch after the restart wrote FABRICATED author
lists onto all five of its admissions, and stamped them
`verification_status='VERIFIED'`, `verified_by_tool='crossref'`,
`verification_method='tool'`, `metadata_quality='COMPLETE'`.

The retrieval had genuinely happened — the reference counts stored alongside match
Crossref exactly, and those numbers exist nowhere but that payload. The author
array was in the same JSON object and was overwritten from memory.

Nothing could detect it, for one structural reason:

    verification_method='tool' was a SELF-ASSERTION WITH NO ARTEFACT BEHIND IT.

No gate could tell an executed retrieval from a claimed one, because the evidence
of the retrieval was never kept. Finding it took an adversarial pass and five
agents. With the payload on disk it is a one-line diff.

Owner ruling, 2026-08-19: "the repository has more than enough room to store
scratchpad logs if they're ever needed. it is very unlikely we will ever have to
look through them unless we are auditing for fidelity."

That is exactly the value profile of this log — near-zero read frequency, and
irreplaceable in the one case that matters.

USE
---
    from retrieval_log import fetch
    payload = fetch("https://api.crossref.org/works/10.xxxx/yyy", session=S,
                    purpose="crossref metadata for REF-00965")

`fetch` returns the parsed JSON *and* writes the raw bytes under
`retrieval-log/<session>/`, with a manifest line recording url, sha256, byte
count, HTTP status, and the UTC timestamp. Writes happen BEFORE the caller sees
the data, so a caller cannot log a different payload than the one it acted on.
`fetch` returns None -- but STILL writes the artefact and manifest line -- for a
non-2xx status as well as for a transport failure or an unparseable body: a 404
or a publisher interstitial is retrieved evidence of a failed retrieval, not
absence of evidence, and CLAUDE.md 5(c) is the reason that distinction is kept
rather than dropped along with the rest of the failure.

    python3 scripts/research/retrieval_log.py --verify-authors --session <id>

verifies stored authors against the LOGGED payload — offline, no network, and
authoritative as-of-retrieval rather than as-of-audit. That distinction matters:
re-fetching at audit time cannot detect a record that was correct when written and
has since been corrected upstream, nor can it run when the API is unreachable.
"""

import argparse
import codecs
import hashlib
import html
import json
import os

GUIDEBOOK_DB_PATH=$D python3 scripts/db.py log-search --parameter 5 --language EN --engine pubmed --depth-method scoping --session $SESS --target-tier 1 --target-evidence-type clinical --target-scope intrinsic --origin planned \
 --query-text 'eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov PubMed: wheelchair AND (turning space OR turning radius OR maneuvering space) AND (dimensions OR anthropometry OR clearance)' \
 --prior-expectation 'Stated in the session transcript before the search ran: 5-25 hits; at most 1-2 usable measurement studies; the US anthropometry report (Steinfeld et al. 2010) may not be indexed in PubMed; full text unlikely.' \
 --results-found 4 --results-screened 4 --results-admitted 0 --saturation-signal partial \
 --findings-note 'Four hits, three on topic: Koontz 2010 (PMID 20434614, T1 case series, n=223, minimum passageway widths for L-turn, 360-degree turn and U-turn); Steinfeld 2010 (PMID 20402047, international comparison of anthropometry and standards); King 2011 (PMID 21657823, scooter three-point-turn areas). One off topic (PMID 36038463, a Delphi study of the word wheelchair-bound). None admitted: Europe PMC reports no open full text for Koontz or Steinfeld (isOpenAccess N, inPMC N), and the abstracts state no dimension, so an admission would add no extractable figure. Koontz and King DOIs are held as RETIRED stash rows (REF-00784, REF-00972): a re-admission cross-files to those ids. Query shape: well-formed; PubMed parsed turning space as turning AND space. Count 4 is below the prior floor of 5; the shortfall reads as an indexing fact (the main US report is not in PubMed), not a query-shape failure.' \
 --result-artefact $R/03b530d696d0a399.json 2>&1 | tail -4
GUIDEBOOK_DB_PATH=$D python3 scripts/db.py log-search --parameter 9 --language EN --engine pubmed --depth-method scoping --session $SESS --target-tier 1 --target-evidence-type co1 --target-scope intrinsic --origin planned \
 --query-text 'eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov PubMed: (wheelchair OR "people with disabilities") AND (doorway OR "door width" OR "corridor width") AND (participatory OR "focus group" OR "lived experience")' \
 --prior-expectation 'Stated in the session transcript before the search ran: 0-3 hits, none qualifying as Co-1; if empty, the likelier cause is three AND-ed concept groups rather than genuine absence.' \
 --results-found 1 --results-screened 1 --results-admitted 0 --saturation-signal none \
 --findings-note 'ZERO-YIELD for Co-1: the one hit (PMID 18002971, Cooper et al. 2007, robotics for personal mobility) reports focus-group participants naming doorways as a barrier but is an engineering overview, not a participatory dimension study; not a Co-1 source for a door or corridor width and not admitted. R14 diagnosis: QUERY-SHAPE FAILURE, not genuine absence. Three AND-ed concept groups; PubMed does not index participatory design-standard work from disabled persons organisations, which publishes as grey reports. A Co-1 retrieval for door and corridor widths is NOT done by this batch and stays open.' \
 --result-artefact $R/6eeeae910085174c.json 2>&1 | tail -4

cat > sessions/session_2026-11-06-pipeline-batch.md <<'EOF'
# Pipeline batch: catalogue readings of two held codes against parameters 4, 5, 6, 8, 9 and 11

**Session id:** `session_2026-11-06-pipeline-batch`
**Branch:** `ccr-f9662223-3a0e7g`
**Session kind:** research (rows only). No schema, script or check change. Tooling gaps found are listed in section 4 and not patched (CLAUDE.md rule 10).
**Pointers:** `sessions/LATEST` and `sessions/LATEST-RESEARCH` move to this session.

**Derive every figure.** Re-run the command beside a number rather than trust the sentence.

## 1. What this session did

The request was "perform a pipeline batch", with no scope. The reading taken: parameters 4 to 11 held rows from one source only (the Singapore code), and the catalogue reading owed on each admitted source (R16) had been recorded for five sources. This batch read two sources already admitted and already persisted, UK Approved Document M volume 2 (REF-00992) and the 2010 ADA Standards (REF-00987), against those parameters. No source was admitted.

- Rows: `select parameter_id, ref_id, count(*) from source_value_extractions where created_by_session = 'session_2026-11-06-pipeline-batch' group by 1, 2`.
- Parameters 7 and 10 (reverberation time, colour temperature): no value found in either source. Parameter 5: ADA 304.3.1 only. The UK text states a 1500 mm square at an entrance landing (2.7(d)) and before a lifting device (3.28(a)) but calls neither a turning space, so neither is filed on parameter 5.
- Searches: two PubMed searches for the turning-space and door-width anchors (executions 197, 198), and after the critic's report two looser shapes (199, 200). Candidates 150 to 155 are staged `PENDING-VERIFICATION` on abstracts only; none was admitted because Europe PMC reports no open full text for the two main anchors and the abstracts state no dimension. The Koontz 2010 and King 2011 DOIs are RETIRED stash rows (REF-00784, REF-00972): an admission cross-files to those ids. The Steinfeld 2010 DOI sits on two unrelated stash rows (REF-00059, REF-00192, GAP-008), so its cross-filing id is not settled.

## 2. The adversarial pass and what it changed

Pass 8, a read-only critic against commit `dd07c9df`: fourteen sustained findings, four survived, one withheld for the owner. Dispositions are in `adversarial_findings` (`select finding_id, lens, severity, disposition from adversarial_findings where pass_id = 8`). The substantive ones: the search that surfaced a harm statement about the US turning-space figure did not carry the flag; the first scan declared headroom and turning absent from the UK text on a keyword search that missed the figures' own spellings (2.1 m, 1.5 m); six parameter 4 and 11 figures were left unextracted; an exec 198 diagnosis named one cause and argued another. All were repaired by a second migration, except two, below.

- **Lens (finding 147), PROVISIONAL-DISPUTED.** Rows 168 to 186 carry lenses that are inconsistent across the two sources (the ADA door and turning rows are `MOB` though their clauses name no population; the UK door-force rows are `MOB` alone though para 2.9 also names limited strength, which no identity code covers). No writer changes a lens column and a second row would duplicate the figure. The lens is the reader's filing, and judgment re-keys it.
- **Gate scope (finding 153), PROVISIONAL-DISPUTED.** `research_batch_dod.py` reads neither `source_scans` nor `source_value_extractions`; COMPLIANT here examined two searches and the candidates, not the nineteen original content rows. It is cited as nothing more than that.
- **Extraction 183 (ADA 1525 mm) stays `contested = 0`.** Exec 197 now carries `harm_finding`; no writer amends `contested`, and the harm statement is an abstract-level hypothesis. Candidate 150's own `harm_finding` is 0 and no writer raises it.
- **Candidate 151's title reads "D Souza"** (the payload is `D'Souza`). No writer amends a title; the correction is on the row's note.
- **Not closed.** `close-adversarial-pass` was not run. Finding 160 is withheld for the owner (section 4).

## 3. Disclosures

- The prior on searches 197 and 198 is stated in the transcript before they ran; `log-search` wrote it with the results, so it is not independently timestamped. The priors on searches 199 and 200 were written after the critic reported their hit counts and say so.
- The scans are `pre-screen` readings of a derived text, located by keyword and by clause number; neither document was read end to end, and diagrams and figures (images) were not read. Scans 6 and 7 are superseded in part by scans 8 and 9 (same source, same mode); the notes of the later scan say what changed.
- Every extraction is `skim`, `preliminary`.
- The UK Approved Document says "For use in England" on its first pages; the rows carry `UK`, the only spelling the jurisdiction vocabulary allows.
- The new UK width and height rows in metres (1.5 m, 2.1 m) will not compose with millimetre rows from other sources until the engine owns a length family (GAP-072).
- No Co-1 retrieval for door or corridor width was done. Exec 198 is a query-shape failure and not an absence; exec 200 shows the index holds on-topic work.
- The Europe PMC checks that support "no open full text" are persisted (`retrieval-log/session_2026-11-06-pipeline-batch/198b3da3fb3d7b6a.json`, `c4c1f76df9877588.json`) but cannot be linked to exec 197: the writer requires the search's query text to name the same host.

## 4. For the owner

1. Whether an instrument for England only (the Approved Document) should be representable below `UK` in the jurisdiction vocabulary (finding 160, WITHHELD-FOR-OWNER).
2. Tooling gaps, none patched: the DoD gate does not read extractions or scans (finding 153); `amend-extraction` cannot change a lens column; no writer raises a candidate's `harm_finding` or corrects a candidate's title; `amend-search --add-result-artefact` cannot link a Europe PMC payload to a PubMed search. They are not filed as GAP rows here (a gap row ships with research rows, and these are tooling), and are named so the owner can decide which to file.
3. Full-text retrieval for the three anthropometry anchors (candidates 150, 151, 152 and 153): none is reachable from this environment; a library route is the owner's.
EOF

input.body:
## Summary

A research-only batch (rows, no schema, script or check change). It reads two already-admitted, already-persisted codes, UK Approved Document M volume 2 (REF-00992) and the 2010 ADA Standards (REF-00987), against parameters 4 to 11, which held rows from one source (Singapore) only. No source is admitted.

- 25 `source_value_extractions` rows (`select parameter_id, ref_id, count(*) from source_value_extractions where created_by_session = 'session_2026-11-06-pipeline-batch' group by 1, 2`). All are `skim`, `preliminary`, quoted verbatim against the persisted payloads.
- Four PubMed searches (executions 197 to 200), six candidates staged `PENDING-VERIFICATION` on abstracts only. Nothing admitted: no open full text for the main anthropometry anchors and the abstracts state no dimension.
- Four scans; scans 8 and 9 replace parts of scans 6 and 7.
- Adversarial pass 8 (read-only critic against `dd07c9df`): 13 sustained, 4 survived, 1 not attacked, 1 withheld for the owner. Eleven are REPAIRED by the second migration; two are PROVISIONAL-DISPUTED. The pass is recorded and closed.

## Not fixed, named

- Lens on the first 19 rows is inconsistent across the two sources and no writer changes a lens column (finding 147, PROVISIONAL-DISPUTED).
- `research_batch_dod.py` reads neither `source_scans` nor `source_value_extractions`, so COMPLIANT examined none of the original content rows (finding 153).
- Extraction 183 (ADA 1525 mm) stays `contested = 0`; exec 197 now carries `harm_finding`.
- Owner question (finding 160): should an England-only instrument be representable below `UK`?
- `test_scan_contract` G01 and G02 are red on untouched `origin/main` as well.

## Gates

`scripts/preflight.sh`: PASS (54 green, 4 nothing-in-scope, 9 advisory failures; two of those are the pre-existing `test_scan_contract` pair above). `research_batch_dod.py --session` COMPLIANT; `adversarial_pass_audit.py` PASS. `git diff --shortstat origin/main -- scripts schemas .github skills ':!scripts/migrations'` is empty.

Session record: `sessions/session_2026-11-06-pipeline-batch.md`. Attestation: `attestations/sessions_session_2026-11-06-pipeline-batch.json` (DEVIATION-LOGGED).

content.text:
The batch is done and PR #211 is open. I unsubscribed from the PR per CLAUDE.md rule 9, so I'm not watching it.

You gave no scope, so I took the first reasonable reading. [ASSUMPTION: "pipeline batch" means a research batch of rows only, no tooling. Basis: parameters 4–11 held rows from one source (Singapore) and only 5 of 58 sources had a catalogue scan.] I read two sources already admitted and persisted, UK Approved Document M vol. 2 (REF-00992) and the 2010 ADA Standards (REF-00987), against parameters 4, 5, 6, 8, 9 and 11. No source was admitted.

- **Rows:** 25 extractions (UK 19, US 6), each quoted verbatim against the persisted text and filed as `skim`, `preliminary`. Parameters 7 and 10 had no value in either source.
- **Searches:** four PubMed searches (executions 197–200). Six candidates are staged `PENDING-VERIFICATION` on abstracts only. None was admitted: Europe PMC reports no open full text for the two main anthropometry anchors, and no abstract states a dimension.
- **Adversarial pass 8:** a read-only critic returned 13 sustained findings, 4 survived, and 1 was withheld for you. I repaired 11 with a second migration. The two I could not repair are recorded as disputed, and the pass is closed.
  - The critic caught that my first scan called headroom and turning space absent from the UK text, on a keyword search that could not have matched "2.1m". It also found that the harm statement about the US turning-space figure had no flag.
- **Gates:**
  - `scripts/preflight.sh` passes.
  - The batch gate (`research_batch_dod.py`) reads COMPLIANT, but it reads neither scans nor extractions, so it says nothing about the original 19 content rows.
  - `adversarial_pass_audit.py` passes.
  - Two `test_scan_contract` failures (G01, G02) are red on untouched `origin/main` as well.
  - The change to `scripts/`, `schemas/`, `.github/` and `skills/` is nil.

[UNVERIFIED] I did not run `run_checks.py --selftest` (no rename occurred). I did not run `preflight.sh --all`.

Not fixed, for you:
1. **Lens:** the lens is inconsistent across the first 19 rows. The ADA door, corridor and turning rows are `MOB`, though their clauses name no population. No writer can change a lens column, so I recorded the finding as disputed.
2. **Contested flag:** extraction 183 (ADA 1525 mm) stays `contested = 0`. Search 197 now carries the harm flag, but no writer raises a candidate's flag or `contested`.
3. **England-only instruments:** should an instrument for England alone be representable below `UK` in the jurisdiction vocabulary? The Approved Document says "For use in England"; the rows carry `UK`.
4. **Full texts:** none of the anthropometry anchors (Koontz 2010, Steinfeld 2010, King 2011) is reachable from this environment. A library route is yours.

The session record is `sessions/session_2026-11-06-pipeline-batch.md`.
